title: Builder Signals · 2026-07-25
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 27 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 11 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex & ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI's Codex/ChatGPT lead Thibault spent the week hyping voice + task capability in the ChatGPT desktop app, explicitly framing it against sci-fi's Jarvis / Samantha / TARS—the goal being to do your best work away from the keyboard. Paired with a recruiting post ("From Science Fiction to Science Reality") that cleared 1K engagements, the signal is clear: OpenAI is betting on desktop agents + voice as the next battleground.
featured.insightZh: OpenAI 的 Codex/ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault 这周在为 ChatGPT 桌面端的语音+任务能力造势，明确把方向对标科幻里的 Jarvis / Samantha / TARS——目标是让你离开键盘、用嘴把最重要的工作干完。配合的招人贴（"From Science Fiction to Science Reality"）互动过千，信号很清楚：OpenAI 正把「桌面 Agent + 语音交互」当作下一代主战场，键盘不再是唯一入口。

featured.title: Peter Yang · 实用 AI 教程与访谈创作者
featured.summaryEn: Peter Yang is testing ChatGPT Voice's multi-threading—spinning up multiple voice threads so a full "AI team" talks both to him and to each other. His feedback is grounded: it should notify him when a thread finishes while others run, and the Chinese pronunciation is still bad. This kind of first-hand dogfooding sketches out a rough-but-directional new pattern: voice-agent orchestration.
featured.insightZh: Peter Yang 在实测 ChatGPT 语音的多线程能力，设想是同时开多个语音线程，让一整支「AI 团队」既跟你说话、也互相对话。他给的产品反馈很接地气：多线程时应该在某个线程干完活时主动通知我；另外中文发音还很糟。这类第一手 dogfooding 反馈值得关注——它勾勒出「语音 Agent 编排」这个还很粗糙但方向明确的新交互形态。

featured.title: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman 谈「史上最大芯片」
featured.summaryEn: Speed has become AI's main battleground—faster inference means more productivity, and Cerebras bets a whole-wafer chip (58x larger than a GPU) is the optimal path for inference, while Feldman argues CUDA is no longer NVIDIA's moat. Cerebras cofounder/CEO Andrew Feldman built the largest chip in computing history and just pulled off the biggest semiconductor IPO ever, plus a $20B+ OpenAI deal. Rather than headlines, this episode builds from "what is a wafer" up to how AI inference works at the silicon level. The core thesis is speed: around mid-2025 AI became genuinely useful, and once you use it, speed is everything—measured as tokens/second/user. His Netflix analogy: when the internet was slow Netflix mailed DVDs; when it got fast it didn't mail DVDs more efficiently, it became a movie studio. Speed unlocks new forms, not just faster old ones—and in multi-turn agentic flows, waiting is…
featured.insightZh: 速度已经成为 AI 的主战场——推理越快越有生产力，Cerebras 用一整片晶圆（比 GPU 大 58 倍）押注「大芯片做推理」是最优解，而 Feldman 认为 CUDA 已不再是英伟达的护城河。 Cerebras 联合创始人兼 CEO Andrew Feldman 造出了计算机史上最大的芯片，并刚完成史上最大的半导体 IPO，还拿下 200 亿美元级别的 OpenAI 大单。这期不谈头条，而是从「什么是晶圆」讲起，一步步搭到硅片层面的 AI 推理原理。 核心论点是「速度」：2025 年中前后 AI 突然从「聪明的玩具」变成真正好用、有人愿意用，一旦要用，速度就是一切——衡量指标是「每用户每秒 token 数」。他用 Netflix 类比：互联网慢的时候 Netflix 邮寄 DVD，网络变快后它没有把邮寄 DVD 做得更高效，而是变成了电影公司。速度不是让旧体验提速，而是解锁全新形态。在 Agent 多轮场景里等待被放大，所以「快得像实时」才是关键 UX。 他还讲了「沙漠中的十年」——2020 年他们解决了没人解决过的问题、交付了产品，却"没人在乎"，所有人说他们疯了。以及为什么 CUDA 不再是护城河：从 GPU 迁到 Cerebras 云上只要八次按键。最后一段谈到 AI 正在瓦解 SaaS——你让 AI「造个类似 Salesforce 的工具」，30 秒就能得到一个能用的工具，跨越组织内部数据孤岛的难题被直接抹平。

items.title: Claude (Anthropic) · 官方账号
items.summaryEn: Anthropic officially announced a major Claude voice upgrade: voice conversations now run on Claude's more capable models (Opus and Sonnet) and can reach your connected tools (email, calendar) mid-conversation. It adds Spanish, French, Hindi, Japanese and more, on every plan, rolling out today in public beta across mobile, desktop, and web. The top tweet hit ~9K engagements—pushing voice from toy toward a genuine productivity entry point.
items.insightZh: Anthropic 官方宣布 Claude 语音模式重大升级：现在语音对话跑在 Claude 更强的模型上（含 Opus 和 Sonnet），并能在对话中途调用你已连接的工具（邮箱、日历等）。同时新增西班牙语、法语、印地语、日语等多语言支持，全计划可用，今日起在移动/桌面/网页公测滚动上线。最高一条互动近 9000——把「更强模型 + 工具调用 + 多语言」塞进语音，是把语音从玩具推向真正生产力入口的关键一步。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad dropped a concrete cost number: Autoscale deployments—typically the most expensive part of scaled apps—are down 80%. He also shared a sharper user story: Viktor first disrupted the agency model with Replit and made money, then figured "why not automate the whole thing, not just the coding," turning the entire agency into an agent loop and asking Replit for an MCP. A concrete slice of AI reshaping services-business models.
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad 甩出一个实打实的成本数据：Autoscale 部署——通常是规模化应用里最贵的一环——成本降了 80%。他还分享了一个更有意思的用户故事：Viktor 先用 Replit 颠覆了传统代理商（agency）模式赚了钱，然后进一步想「为什么不把整件事自动化，而不只是写代码」，于是把整个 agency 变成一个 agent loop，找 Replit 团队要了个 MCP。这是「AI 重构服务业商业模式」的具体切片。

items.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人）
items.summaryEn: Madhu Guru raised a sharp enterprise-security question: after the GPT Sol incident, he talked with a public-company security lead—when identity and access management (IAM) was designed for a *finite* number of employees, how do you manage effectively *infinite* agents? One employee may sit behind a swarm of agents, each needing credentials and access. A governance blind spot that surfaces inevitably as agents scale, with few mature answers today.
items.insightZh: Madhu Guru 抛出一个企业安全的尖锐问题：在 GPT Sol 事件之后，他跟一位上市公司安全负责人聊——当身份与访问管理（IAM）本是为「有限数量员工」设计时，你如何管理「事实上无限数量」的 Agent？一个员工可能背后挂着一堆 Agent，每个都需要凭据和权限。这是随着 Agent 规模化必然浮现、但当前几乎没有成熟答案的治理盲区，MD 级别做企业 AI 落地时值得提前布局。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Garry Tan ran two threads this week: continuing to push for SF housing and CEQA reform (the regulatory tool NIMBYs abuse to block housing across California), framing "build it" as an urban-renewal cause; and stating plainly that "open weight models are very very important." For AI ecosystem/policy watchers the latter matters—an institution YC's size publicly backing open weights shifts early-founder tech choices.
items.insightZh: Garry Tan 这周两条主线：一是持续为旧金山住房建设与 CEQA 改革发声（NIMBY 用来阻挠加州各地建房的监管工具），把「建起来」当作城市复兴命题；二是明确表态"开放权重模型非常非常重要"。对关注 AI 生态与政策的人，后者尤其值得记——YC 这种体量的机构公开站队开源权重，会影响一批早期创业者的技术选型。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Rauch shared two platform updates: Python code now cold-starts 2x faster on Vercel, automatically, no user changes; and the AI Gateway keeps improving at what he calls "unreal product velocity." For teams shipping AI apps, faster Python cold-starts directly affect agent/inference UX on serverless—the kind of low-level optimization that's a hidden lever on production cost and latency.
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Rauch 报了两条平台侧进展：Python 代码在 Vercel 上冷启动速度自动翻倍（2x faster），无需用户改动；AI Gateway 持续迭代、团队产品速度他形容"不真实"。对做 AI 应用工程落地的团队，Python 冷启动提速直接影响 Serverless 场景下的 Agent/推理服务体验——这类底层优化往往是生产环境成本与延迟的隐形杠杆。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie offered a framework for AI and people: AI is best understood as a force multiplier for fields you already know, or an accelerator for one you want to learn. He flags a third category—no existing judgment, no interest in developing it—that will mostly produce slop and won't drive much real value. A useful screen for leaders running AI transformation: AI amplifies judgment, it doesn't replace it.
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 给了一个关于 AI 与人的判断框架：AI 最好被理解为「你已有领域的力量放大器」，或「你想学新领域的加速器」。他点出第三类人——既无既有判断力、也无兴趣去培养判断力的人——基本只会产出 slop（垃圾内容），且不会带来多少真实价值。对管理团队做 AI 转型的人，这句是很有用的甄别标准：AI 放大的是判断力，不是替代判断力。

items.title: Peter Steinberger · OpenClaw / OpenAI（ClawFather）
items.summaryEn: Peter Steinberger (a core figure in the OpenClaw ecosystem) shared a pragmatic engineering detail: after seeing certain behavior, they added code paths that call the claude CLI directly—"hard to fight the system." This kind of tradeoff—flowing with underlying tools' existing behavior rather than forcing an abstraction—is a recurring real-world lesson when building multi-agent/multi-model orchestration, useful for teams building agent platforms.
items.insightZh: Peter Steinberger（OpenClaw 生态核心人物）分享了一个很务实的工程细节：他们观察到某些情况后，加了直接调用 claude CLI 的代码路径——"很难跟系统对着干"。这类"顺着底层工具的既有行为走、而不是硬造抽象"的取舍，是构建多 Agent/多模型编排系统时反复出现的现实教训，对做 Agent 平台的工程团队有参考价值。

items.title: Claude Code 现已支持 Artifacts
items.summaryEn: Anthropic announced artifacts in Claude Code: it captures a session's work progress as live, shareable visual pages—PR walkthroughs, system explainers, dashboards, release checklists—that update themselves as the session runs. Artifacts are built from your session's full context (codebase, connectors, conversation), so you don't wire up data sources or stand up infrastructure—you ask for a page and Claude Code builds it from what exists. A common use case is debugging: an engineer kicks off an incident investigation before standup, Claude Code works the logs and publishes an artifact (timeline, suspect commits, error-rate chart), republishing twice by the time standup begins. Every publish is a new version at the same link with version history for rollback. Private to your org by default, viewable only by authenticated members, not publicly shareable, with admin access controls, retenti…
items.insightZh: Anthropic 官宣 Claude Code 新增 artifacts 能力：把一次 session 的工作进度实时沉淀成可分享的可视化网页——PR 讲解、系统说明、仪表盘、发布清单等，会随着 session 推进自动更新。artifact 基于你 session 的完整上下文构建（代码库、连接器、对话本身），无需你手动接数据源或搭基础设施——你只要「要一个页面」，Claude Code 就用现有信息拼出来。典型场景是调试：工程师站会前发起事故调查，Claude Code 跑完日志、发布一个带时间线/可疑提交/错误率图表的 artifact，站会开始前已自动 republish 两次。每次发布都是同一链接下的新版本，带版本历史可回滚。默认对组织私有，仅认证成员可见、不能公开，管理员可做访问控制/保留策略/合规 API 可见性。目前对 Claude Team 和 Enterprise 组织 beta 开放。
